headlines.article_text: SpaceX (SPCX) Q3 2026 earnings report: Live updates Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu watch now VIDEO 2:20 02:20 SpaceX earnings in focus as Starlink growth and AI spending take center stage Morning Call SpaceX is set to announce third-quarter results after the bell on Tuesday, the second earnings report for Elon Musk's defense tech conglomerate since its record IPO in June. Here's what analysts are expecting, according to LSEG consensus estimates: Revenue: $12.72 billion expected Earnings per share: 13 cents expected While SpaceX is best known for its reusable rockets, most of its revenue and profit in recent quarters came from the company's connectivity segment, which consists of its Starlink satellite internet service. Buzz is building about Starlink's plans to build a U.S. mobile network after SpaceX, earlier this month, announced that it's buying 800 MHz of low-band spectrum, and after the Federal Communications Commission approved a plan for the company to build out a 15,000-satellite constellation. The moves strengthen "Starlink Mobile's ability to compete with major carriers by enabling broader, deeper coverage," RBC Capital Markets analysts wrote in a note ahead of earnings. The firm has a $225 price target on SpaceX stock and the equivalent of a buy rating. In the third quarter, analysts are expecting AI revenue of $6.47 billion, connectivity sales of $4.84 billion, and revenue in the space business of $1.41 billion, according to StreetAccount. During the third quarter, SpaceX also closed its $60 billion purchase of AI coding startup Cursor. What you need to know ahead of the earnings report: Capex and AI data center expansion Here's why analysts are bullish on SpaceX heading into the report Tesla-SpaceX merger speculation 3 Min Ago How the stock has done since the IPO SpaceX stock chart. Since opening at $150 on June 12, SpaceX shares have edged slightly lower, slipping to $147.50 on Tuesday. That gives Space a market cap of about $2 trillion. The stock hit a low of $104.83 on Aug. 3, a few days before the first post-IPO lockup expired, making more than 911 million SpaceX shares available for trading. The lockup lifted on Aug. 6, and the stock rallied, popping 6% initially, then nearly 16% the day after. —Lora Kolodny 39 Min Ago Starship hits several milestones, but is still being tested The SpaceX Starship and Super Heavy v3 Booster lift off on its 14th test flight from the SpaceX launch complex in Starbase, Texas, US, September 28, 2026. Steve Nesius | Reuters SpaceX continues to serve as a critical launch provider to the U.S. Defense Department and NASA. The business hasn't been historically profitable, but it's the segment that captured the public's interest in the rocket maker. In the second quarter, SpaceX reported launch revenue of $962 million and a net loss of $542 million. Future profitability hinges on the success of SpaceX's Starship mega-rocket, which is still being developed and tested. Since the company's last earnings call in August, SpaceX hit multiple milestones, reaching orbit and using Starship to deploy dozens of its new V.3 Starlink satellites during Test Flight 14. But the rocket is still far from reliable or reusable. Investors are awaiting an update on pending NASA missions and the future of the older Falcon rocket. SpaceX has reportedly stopped allowing other companies to launch their cargo, including satellites, into orbit on Falcon missions. —Lora Kolodny 1 Hour Ago Capex and the SpaceXAI data center build out A drone view shows the xAI Colossus 2 "Macrohard" data centre in Southaven, Mississippi, U.S., May 30, 2026. Kevin Wurm | Reuters In its first earnings report in August, SpaceX reported capital expenditures of $18.4 billion, with 80% of that going towards its artificial intelligence division. That number spooked Wall Street, and shares dropped following the report. SpaceX and xAI merged in February and the company has been pouring money into its effort to become a major player in AI, a market dominated by OpenAI, Anthropic and Google. The AI division also acquired Cursor in a $60 billion transaction and is now known as either SpaceXAI or SpaceXSI, with the "SI" standing for President Donald Trump's preferred "Super Intelligence." — Lora Kolodny 2 Hours Ago Analysts are bullish on SpaceX ahead of earnings A general view of a SpaceX building on the day of the company’s initial public offering (IPO), in Starbase, Texas, U.S., June 12, 2026. Gabriel V. Cardenas | Reuters Wall Street is sounding bullish on SpaceX ahead of its third-quarter earnings report, to be delivered after the bell on Tuesday. Mizuho has an outperform rating on the stock and a $200 price target, per a Monday note from analyst Brett Linzey. Shares were trading around $148 as of 10:45 a.m. on Tuesday. "AI is the largest swing factor for 3Q26 revenue and EBITDA. Consensus has AI revenue of $6.30B (+146% Q/Q from $2.56B) and AI adj. EBITDA of $3.32B (from $1.15B)," he wrote. Analysts are expecting some conversation about deals or competitive plays with cable and telecom companies following SpaceX's acquisition of low-band spectrum earlier this month. "We expect initial strategic commentary centers around Connectivity and how SPCX can partner/compete its way into global markets, although we think low-band distribution becomes a meaningful intelligence lever over time," Colin Canfield at Cantor Fitzgerald wrote in a Monday note. He has a price target of $246 and an overweight rating on the stock. Oppenheimer's expectations are more measured. The bank thinks the quarter will be "in-line" with "guidance reiterated." "Industry subscriber growth is slowing with limited room for pricing action, so focus is shifting from net adds and service revenue growth toward cost-cutting using AI, and lower subsidies/churn," Timothy Horan at Oppenheimer told clients in a Tuesday note. He expects "more rational incumbent behavior" from SpaceX's competitors. –Tobias Burns 3 Hours Ago Musk says he's giving stock to U.S. kids watch now VIDEO 1:53 01:53 Elon Musk vows to donate SpaceX shares to every child in America The Exchange Musk said Monday that he'll give every child in the U.S. one of his SpaceX shares next year. With 72 million children under 18 in the U.S. as of July 1, 2025, according to official census data, that would amount a giveaway of about $10.5 billion worth of shares as of the current price. Musk, the world's richest person with a net worth of over $900 billion, said in a post on X that, "This will be the first of many," without providing further details. However, when it comes to fulfilling his philanthropic promises , Musk has a spotty track record. —Ari Levy 4 Hours Ago Starshield issues in Ukraine Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy holds a press conference during the second day of the European Union leaders' summit in Brussels, Belgium, on October 16, 2026. Dursun Aydemir | Anadolu | Getty Images A military tier of Starlink, marketed as Starshield, has drawn scrutiny of late as restrictions on the system in Ukraine hindered the country's ability to defend itself against intensifying attacks by Russia. Ukrainian officials said SpaceX and the Trump administration restricted Starshield without warning last week, causing Ukraine's military forces to lose control of drones moving over 100 miles per hour, as the craft were relying on Starshield for connectivity at those speeds. Musk said in a post on X that any changes to Starshield should be attributed to the U.S. government and President Donald Trump, though Trump later denied he ordered any such restrictions. Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told NBC's "Meet the Press" on Sunday that the restraints remained in place over the weekend. headlines.article_text: Stocks making the biggest moves midday: HAS, NOC, EFX, GM Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Check out the companies making the biggest moves midday: Hasbro — Shares gained more than 5% after the toymaker reported better-than-expected results for the third quarter. Hasbro also raised its revenue growth outlook for the full year. Northrop Grumman — Shares jumped nearly 5% after the defense contractor reported results for the third quarter. The company earned $7.89 per share, beating an LSEG estimate of $7.18 per share. However, revenue of $11.12 billion was just below the $11.14 billion consensus. Equifax – Shares of the consumer credit bureau leapt almost 12%. Equifax earned $2.26 per share on an adjusted basis in the third quarter, beating the FactSet consensus of $2.20. Revenue of $1.69 billion was in line with expectations. The company dialed back its revenue guidance for 2026, however. Dream Finders Homes — Shares rose more than 8% after the homebuilder completed the acquisition of Beazer Homes that was announced Aug. 7. Arcus Biosciences — Shares gained more than 8% after Arcus shared data from its trial of casdatifan, a treatment for a type of kidney cancer. In this latest study, the company found that patients can benefit from the drug across all lines of therapy. General Motors — The automaker's stock fell nearly 7% despite GM reporting third-quarter numbers that beat analyst expectations. headlines.summary: GM narrowed its 2026 earnings guidance and raised its adjusted automotive free cash flow outlook after beating Wall Street’s third-quarter estimates.
headlines.article_text: General Motors (GM) earnings Q3 2026 Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points General Motors beat Wall Street’s expectations on the top- and bottom-lines. The Detroit automaker raised its free cash flow expectations and narrowed its 2026 full-year guidance. GM also announced a new multiyear stock buyback of $20 billion, but didn’t give a specific timeframe for the repurchase. In this article GM Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 7:11 07:11 GM CFO Paul Jacobson on $20B stock buyback: Driven by our stellar free cash flow generation Squawk Box DETROIT — General Motors narrowed its 2026 earnings guidance and raised its free cash flow expectations after beating Wall Street's third-quarter expectations. The Detroit automaker also announced a new multiyear stock buyback of $20 billion after GM completed a $6 billion share repurchase program that was announced in January. GM did not disclose a specific time to complete the program. Despite the positive news, GM stock was off roughly 5% during trading Tuesday as the company's outlook missed Wall Street's expectations. Wall Street analysts were mixed before the report on whether GM would raise its guidance Tuesday amid concerns of slowing sales and rising commodity costs. Analysts' expectations included a midpoint of $13.41 per share for the year compared with GM's new $13.25 per share midpoint, according to LSEG. Several analysts in investor notes Tuesday said GM's third-quarter results were solid, but raised concerns about whether higher costs and pressures on vehicle pricing would limit earnings growth next year. Here's how GM performed in the third quarter, compared with average estimates compiled by LSEG: Earnings per share: $3.70 adjusted vs. $3.63 expected Revenue: $50.02 billion vs. $48.7 billion expected GM's new guidance includes adjusted earnings before interest and taxes of between $14.5 billion and $15.5 billion, or $12.75 to $13.75 adjusted earnings per share, and adjusted automotive free cash flow of between $11.5 billion and $12.5 billion. That compares with its raised guidance from July that included adjusted EBIT of between $14 billion and $16 billion, or $12 to $14 adjusted EPS, and adjusted automotive free cash flow of $9.5 billion to $11.5 billion. "I think the market's been pretty consistent from what we've said all year," GM CFO Paul Jacobson told CNBC's Phil LeBeau . "Our fourth quarter's going to be down sequentially. ... I think the fact that we're able to hold our guidance in the face of that late inflationary pressure in the year is another sign of the GM team executing really well." Mary Barra, chair and chief executive officer of General Motors Co., during a news conference at the Hudson's building in Detroit, Michigan, US, on Monday, April 15, 2024. Jeff Kowalsky | Bloomberg | Getty Images GM on Tuesday said it expects commodity inflation costs to be around $2 billion, which was the high end of its previous guidance. That includes higher costs for logistics and dynamic random-access memory, or DRAM, chips that are impacting multiple industries . While the inflationary costs were at the automaker's high end of guidance, GM said its gross tariff costs are expected to be at the low end of its expected $2.5 billion to $3.5 billion range. Warranty costs are expected to be at high end between $1 billion and $1.5 billion, GM said. Jacobson said vehicle pricing is relatively flat as inflationary costs continue to increase. He said the company would assess where consumers are in the coming year when deciding if it should pass costs along by raising prices more than normal. "GM is performing well, and we are working hard to continue our momentum despite growing inflationary pressures through strategic investments in new products and services, and through improved quality and operating efficiency," GM CEO Mary Barra said Tuesday in a letter to shareholders. The automaker also said the costs of its pullback in all-electric vehicles announced last year were "substantially completed," saying it has recorded $11.2 billion in such charges since the second half of last year, including paying $4.6 billion of $7.4 billion in cash through the third quarter. The company's net income attributed to stockholders was $3.3 billion during the third quarter, up roughly $2 billion from a year earlier. GM's North American operations continued to lead the automaker's results, accounting for $3.6 billion of its $4.1 billion in adjusted EBIT results during the third quarter. GM's 2025 third-quarter results included $48.59 billion in revenue, net income attributable to stockholders of $1.3 billion and earnings per share of $2.80 adjusted.
